meta.notes: Passed is a silent runtime outcome, not a severity. MCA-validate flags borderline severities for compliance-admin review. Rules with 'held'/'Step 2.4' in notes are document-dependent (Form 244/801) and stay Confirm until pilot validation.

rules.rule_name: RECO Information Guide provided and explained before agreement
rules.requirement: Before providing services to a client (or assistance to a self-represented party), the agent must give the person a copy of the RECO Information Guide and explain its contents. The guide must be provided before a representation agreement is entered into.
rules.applies_when: Any deal with a client or self-represented party.
rules.detection_signal: No legislated acknowledgement exists, and provision usually occurs via RECO's electronic tool outside the deal package — not verifiable from the documents.
rules.finding_template: Confirm the RECO Information Guide step.
rules.confirm_text: Before providing services or assistance, I gave a copy of the RECO Information Guide to the prospective client (or self-represented party) and explained its contents, before any representation agreement was entered into.
rules.fix_guidance: Provide and explain the RECO Information Guide before entering an agreement or providing assistance; keep the RECO tool's email confirmation as evidence.
rules.pinpoint: O. Reg. 567/05 s.13 (guide content); provide/explain obligation — TRESA Act [legal-review]
rules.notes: No legislated acknowledgement; some brokerages require one as policy. Overlaps the self-represented-party form (2.4-02).

rules.rule_name: A representation agreement is present for each client
rules.requirement: Services may only be provided to a client under a representation agreement with the brokerage; a brokerage must not enter an agreement to trade in real estate that does not include representation.
rules.applies_when: The brokerage represents a buyer and/or seller in the trade.
rules.detection_signal: A signed representation agreement (listing agreement for the seller; buyer representation agreement for the buyer) is present in the package for each represented party.
rules.finding_template: A signed representation agreement does not appear to be on file for one of the represented parties. Services can only be provided under a representation agreement.
rules.fix_guidance: Ensure a signed representation agreement is in place for each client before submitting to your brokerage.
rules.pinpoint: O. Reg. 567/05 s.13.5 (seller), s.13.6 (buyer); TRESA Act representation-required [legal-review]
rules.notes: Related to 2.6-01 (no customer agreements). Buyer-side agreements are the more common gap.

rules.rule_name: Representation type is identifiable
rules.requirement: Representation is either brokerage representation or designated representation; the agreement reflects which form applies.
rules.applies_when: A representation agreement is present.
rules.detection_signal: The agreement indicates brokerage vs designated representation (and, if designated, names the designated representative(s)).
rules.finding_template: The form of representation (brokerage or designated) isn't clearly identifiable in the agreement. Confirm which applies.
rules.fix_guidance: Ensure the agreement clearly reflects whether it is brokerage or designated representation.
rules.notes: Supports multiple-representation detection in Category 3. Designated-rep content specifics are checked in 2.3-11.

rules.rule_name: Effective date present
rules.requirement: The agreement must clearly state the date it takes effect.
rules.applies_when: A representation agreement is present.
rules.detection_signal: An effective date on the agreement.
rules.finding_template: The representation agreement is missing an effective date. Confirm it is present.
rules.fix_guidance: Add the effective date to the agreement.

rules.rule_name: Expiry date present
rules.requirement: The agreement must clearly state the date it expires.
rules.applies_when: A representation agreement is present.
rules.detection_signal: An expiry date on the agreement.
rules.finding_template: The representation agreement is missing an expiry date. Confirm it is present.
rules.fix_guidance: Add the expiry date to the agreement.

rules.rule_name: Required initials and amendments verified
rules.requirement: The expiry date must be displayed prominently on the first page and the client must initial next to it (regardless of duration); more broadly, all required initials must be present and any handwritten amendments must match across the executed documents.
rules.applies_when: A representation agreement is present.
rules.detection_signal: Initials adjacent to the expiry date and at required points; consistency of handwritten amendments across copies. Not reliably machine-detectable on scanned/handwritten packages.
rules.finding_template: Confirm required initials and amendments.
rules.confirm_text: I have verified that all required initials and amendments are present and match across the executed documents.
rules.fix_guidance: Ensure the expiry date is prominent on the first page with the client's initials beside it, and that every required initial and handwritten amendment is present and consistent across copies.
rules.pinpoint: O. Reg. 567/05 s.13.4(1) para 2 (prominent, first page) & para 3 (initialled next to expiry)
rules.notes: Digital-signing platforms enforce fields before envelope close, so the gap applies mainly to handwritten amendments and scanned files → Confirm attestation, logged to the audit trail.

rules.rule_name: Single, non-contradictory expiry date
rules.requirement: The brokerage is responsible for ensuring the agreement contains only one date on which it expires.
rules.applies_when: A representation agreement is present.
rules.detection_signal: More than one conflicting expiry date across the agreement.
rules.finding_template: The agreement appears to contain more than one expiry date. Confirm there is only one.
rules.fix_guidance: Remove any conflicting expiry dates so only one remains.

rules.rule_name: Remuneration method stated
rules.requirement: The agreement must clearly identify the method for determining remuneration payable to the brokerage (fixed amount, percentage of sale/rental price, or a combination — a percentage may be a decreasing series but must be an agreed amount/percentage).
rules.applies_when: A representation agreement is present.
rules.detection_signal: A stated remuneration method.
rules.finding_template: The agreement does not clearly state how the brokerage's remuneration is determined. Confirm the method is specified.
rules.fix_guidance: State the remuneration as a fixed amount, a percentage of the sale/rental price, or a combination.
rules.notes: For seller agreements, also state separately any amount offered toward the buyer's brokerage fees (see 2.3-07 and Category 6).

rules.rule_name: No net-listing / list-minus-sale remuneration basis
rules.requirement: Brokerages are prohibited from any remuneration arrangement based on the difference between the listing price and the actual sale price, and may not charge or collect remuneration computed on that basis.
rules.applies_when: A seller representation (listing) agreement is present.
rules.detection_signal: Remuneration language tied to the difference between list price and sale price.
rules.finding_template: The agreement appears to base remuneration on the difference between the list price and the sale price, which is prohibited. This must be corrected before submitting.
rules.fix_guidance: Replace any list-minus-sale (net listing) remuneration with an agreed amount or percentage of the sale price.
rules.pinpoint: O. Reg. 567/05 s.23; TRESA Act s.33 [legal-review]
rules.notes: Rare but a hard prohibition → Critical.

rules.rule_name: Circumstances that change remuneration are explained
rules.requirement: The agreement must identify any circumstances in which remuneration might change, explain how it might change for each, and indicate whether one or more brokerages may receive remuneration (including seller-side amounts offered toward a buyer's brokerage fees, and multiple-representation scenarios).
rules.applies_when: A representation agreement is present.
rules.detection_signal: Language covering variable-remuneration circumstances and their effect, including any amount offered toward the other side's fees.
rules.finding_template: The agreement may not explain the circumstances in which remuneration could change (for example, multiple representation, or an amount offered toward the buyer's brokerage fees). Review before submitting.
rules.fix_guidance: Spell out each circumstance that could change remuneration, how it changes, and whether one or more brokerages may be paid.
rules.notes: Overlaps Category 6 and 3.3-05 (seller-paid buyer fees).

rules.rule_name: Method for paying remuneration stated
rules.requirement: The agreement should be clear about the method used to pay remuneration owing to the brokerage (e.g., a direction to the client's lawyer; any prohibited methods such as credit card).
rules.applies_when: A representation agreement is present.
rules.detection_signal: A stated payment method for remuneration.
rules.finding_template: The agreement does not clearly state how the brokerage's remuneration will be paid. Confirm the payment method.
rules.fix_guidance: State the method of payment (e.g., a direction to the lawyer handling the transaction).
rules.notes: Listed as required content but administrative — set to Warning as a judgment call; flag for calibration if you want Critical.

rules.rule_name: Description of services present
rules.requirement: The agreement must include a complete, comprehensible description of the services to be provided (in the agreement or a schedule); for a designated representation agreement, the services the designated representative(s) will provide.
rules.applies_when: A representation agreement is present.
rules.detection_signal: A services description in the agreement or an attached schedule.
rules.finding_template: The agreement does not appear to describe the services being provided. Confirm the services are documented.
rules.fix_guidance: Include a complete description of the services in the agreement or a schedule.

rules.rule_name: Termination provisions present
rules.requirement: The agreement must include terms related to termination, including the rights and obligations on termination — and is expected to address what happens if a client declines to consent to multiple representation.
rules.applies_when: A representation agreement is present.
rules.detection_signal: Termination provisions in the agreement.
rules.finding_template: The agreement does not appear to include termination provisions. Confirm they are present.
rules.fix_guidance: Add termination terms, including what happens (and any financial implications) if a client declines multiple-representation consent.
rules.notes: The multiple-representation-decline handling is "expected"; treated here as part of the termination-provisions check.

rules.rule_name: Designated representation agreement required content
rules.requirement: A designated representation agreement must also include: the fact that the brokerage is not providing representation; the name of each designated representative; the services each designated representative will provide; the duties of the brokerage; and the duty of the designated representative(s).
rules.applies_when: The agreement is a designated representation agreement (see 2.2-02).
rules.detection_signal: The five designated-representation content elements.
rules.finding_template: This designated representation agreement may be missing required content (brokerage-not-representing statement, named designated representative(s), their services, brokerage duties, and the designated representative's duty). Review before submitting.
rules.fix_guidance: Add the five designated-representation elements to the agreement.
rules.notes: Only fires for designated representation agreements.

rules.rule_name: Holdover clause explained (if present)
rules.requirement: Holdover clauses are not required, but where present the client should understand their existence, terms, and financial implications, including any effect on the holdover period.
rules.applies_when: A representation agreement containing a holdover clause is present.
rules.detection_signal: A holdover clause and whether its terms are clearly set out.
rules.finding_template: This agreement contains a holdover clause. Confirm its terms and financial implications were clearly explained to the client.
rules.fix_guidance: Ensure the holdover clause's terms and implications are clear and were explained before signing.
rules.notes: Complaint-prone; Warning by nature (not a mandatory element).

rules.rule_name: Subject property / scope identified
rules.requirement: The scope of the agreement must be clear. For a seller client, the agreement must clearly identify the property in question. For a buyer client, the agreement should identify whether services relate to a specific property, geographic area, or property type.
rules.applies_when: A representation agreement is present.
rules.detection_signal: A clearly identified property (seller) or defined scope (buyer).
rules.finding_template: The agreement does not clearly identify the subject property or scope. For a listing agreement this is required.
rules.fix_guidance: Identify the property (seller) or the specific property/area/type scope (buyer) in the agreement.
rules.notes: Property identification is mandatory for seller agreements (Critical); buyer-scope is "should" — softer, flagged for calibration.

rules.rule_name: Self-represented status verified
rules.requirement: Before providing any assistance, the agent must verify the party is, or intends to be, self-represented (not a client of any brokerage).
rules.applies_when: A party on the other side of the trade is unrepresented.
rules.detection_signal: Whether the other party is represented is partly visible on the confirmation-of-cooperation documentation, but intent to self-represent is not.
rules.finding_template: Confirm the self-represented status of the other party.
rules.confirm_text: I verified that this party is, or intends to be, self-represented (not a client of any brokerage) before providing any assistance.
rules.fix_guidance: Confirm the party's representation status before providing assistance.

rules.rule_name: Information and Disclosure to Self-represented Party form present
rules.requirement: Before providing any assistance to a self-represented party, the agent must provide the RECO Information Guide and the Information and Disclosure to Self-represented Party form.
rules.applies_when: A self-represented party is involved in the trade.
rules.detection_signal: A completed Information and Disclosure to Self-represented Party form in the package.
rules.finding_template: This trade appears to involve a self-represented party, but the Information and Disclosure to Self-represented Party form is not on file. It is required before providing assistance.
rules.fix_guidance: Provide the Information and Disclosure to Self-represented Party form (and the RECO Information Guide) and keep it in the file.
rules.notes: Detectable once OREA/RECO forms are loaded (there are designated-rep and brokerage-rep versions of the form).

rules.rule_name: Acknowledgement of the self-represented party form (best efforts)
rules.requirement: The agent must make best efforts to obtain an acknowledgement that the Information and Disclosure to Self-represented Party form was provided, and give the party a copy of their acknowledgement.
rules.applies_when: A self-represented party is involved.
rules.detection_signal: A signed acknowledgement of the self-represented party form.
rules.finding_template: No acknowledgement of the self-represented party form is on file. This is best-efforts — confirm one was requested.
rules.fix_guidance: Obtain the party's acknowledgement and give them a copy.
rules.notes: Best-efforts → Warning.

rules.rule_name: Assistance kept within permitted limits
rules.requirement: Agents must not provide services, opinions, or advice to a self-represented party; any assistance must be a service to (or incidental to a service to) the agent's client, in the client's best interests, and consistent with the client's instructions, and the agent must clearly communicate the required messages.
rules.applies_when: A self-represented party is involved.
rules.detection_signal: Conduct-based; not verifiable from documents.
rules.finding_template: Confirm the limits on assistance to the self-represented party.
rules.confirm_text: I limited my assistance to the self-represented party to what serves my client's best interests and instructions, and I clearly communicated that I represent my client (not them), that I cannot provide them services, opinions, or advice, and that anything they share will be shared with my client.
rules.fix_guidance: Keep assistance within the permitted limits and communicate the required messages.
rules.notes: Conduct attestation; ties to implied-representation risk (2.7-01).

rules.rule_name: Written consent before disclosing confidential client information
rules.requirement: Except as authorized or required by law, brokerages and agents must not disclose confidential client information to a third party without the client's prior written consent.
rules.applies_when: Any trade (confidentiality duty is ongoing, including after the relationship ends).
rules.detection_signal: Disclosures of confidential information are conduct-based and not visible in the package.
rules.finding_template: Confirm the confidentiality rule.
rules.confirm_text: I did not disclose any confidential client information to a third party without the client's prior written consent, except where authorized or required by law.
rules.fix_guidance: Obtain written consent before disclosing confidential client information to a third party.
rules.notes: Designated-representation information-barrier duties are brokerage-policy conduct — not modeled as separate rules (see ambiguities).

rules.rule_name: Confidentiality consent content complete
rules.requirement: A consent to disclose confidential information must give the client enough to make an informed decision and clear written direction, answering: what information will be disclosed; who will receive it; the purpose; and who might benefit and how.
rules.applies_when: A confidentiality/disclosure consent document is present in the package.
rules.detection_signal: The consent covers the four required questions.
rules.finding_template: The consent to disclose confidential information may be missing required content (what is disclosed, to whom, the purpose, and who benefits and how). Review before submitting.
rules.fix_guidance: Ensure the consent answers all four questions in clear written direction.
rules.notes: Only fires when such a consent document is present.

rules.rule_name: No prohibited customer agreement
rules.requirement: Customer relationships and customer agreements are not permitted (effective December 1, 2023); any pre-existing customer agreement automatically expired by March 30, 2024. Services must be under a representation agreement.
rules.applies_when: Any current deal.
rules.detection_signal: A "customer service agreement" or other customer-relationship document (a pre-TRESA form) in the package.
rules.finding_template: This package appears to include a customer agreement, which is no longer permitted. Replace it with a representation agreement.
rules.fix_guidance: Enter a representation agreement with the person and remove the customer agreement.
rules.pinpoint: TRESA Act (customer elimination) [legal-review]; O. Reg. 567/05 transition
rules.notes: Pairs with 2.2-01. Mostly a legacy/edge case now, but a clean deterministic-ish flag.

rules.rule_name: No implied representation created through conduct
rules.requirement: Implied representation can arise when an agent provides services, opinions, or advice (or exchanges confidential information, negotiates, etc.) for a person without a written agreement; agents must avoid creating implied relationships, which can also trigger multiple representation.
rules.applies_when: Any trade involving a non-client (e.g., a self-represented party or a prospective client).
rules.detection_signal: Conduct-based; not verifiable from documents.
rules.finding_template: Confirm you did not create an implied representation agreement.
rules.confirm_text: I did not, through my conduct, create an implied representation agreement with any non-client in this trade; where I assisted a self-represented party, my conduct stayed consistent with the disclosures I made to them.
rules.fix_guidance: Keep interactions with non-clients to factual information and permitted assistance; use a written agreement before providing services, opinions, or advice.
rules.pinpoint: TRESA Act (definition of 'representation agreement') [legal-review]; O. Reg. 365/22
rules.notes: If an implied agreement arose alongside an existing client, it creates multiple representation → Category 3 (3.2) obligations follow.

rules.rule_name: Disclosures in plain language
rules.requirement: Every disclosure, consent, and acknowledgement must be written in plain language that is clear and concise.
rules.applies_when: Any disclosure/consent/acknowledgement document is present.
rules.detection_signal: Readability and clarity of the disclosure documents.
rules.finding_template: One or more disclosure documents may not meet the plain-language requirement. Review for clarity before submitting to your brokerage.
rules.fix_guidance: Rewrite dense or legalistic disclosure text in clear, concise language a consumer can understand.
rules.notes: Subjective; low precision until tuned.

rules.rule_name: Disclosure labelled "disclosure"
rules.requirement: A disclosure must be identified by the prominent placement of the word "disclosure".
rules.applies_when: A document functions as a required disclosure.
rules.detection_signal: Presence of the word "disclosure" as a heading/label on disclosure documents.
rules.finding_template: A required disclosure does not appear to be prominently labelled with the word "disclosure." Confirm the document is properly identified.
rules.fix_guidance: Add a prominent "Disclosure" heading/label to the document so it is clearly identified.
rules.notes: Some brokerages hard-bounce on this — candidate for a per-brokerage severity override.

rules.rule_name: Disclosures presented to draw attention
rules.requirement: Disclosures/consents/acknowledgements must be presented in a manner that draws the person's attention to the required information.
rules.applies_when: Any required disclosure/consent/acknowledgement is present.
rules.detection_signal: Formatting/prominence of the required content.
rules.finding_template: Required disclosure content may be buried or not clearly surfaced. Confirm it is presented prominently.
rules.fix_guidance: Present required information distinctly (headings, spacing, emphasis) so it is not lost in surrounding text.
rules.notes: Overlaps 3.1-01 / 3.1-08; merge candidate.

rules.rule_name: Disclosures are standalone documents
rules.requirement: Required disclosures, consents, and acknowledgements should be distinct and separate from the representation agreement and from any agreement facilitating the transaction.
rules.applies_when: A required disclosure/consent/acknowledgement is in scope.
rules.detection_signal: A required disclosure appears embedded as a clause inside the representation agreement or APS rather than as its own document.
rules.finding_template: A required disclosure appears to be embedded in another agreement rather than provided as a separate document. Consider separating it.
rules.fix_guidance: If a disclosure is embedded inside the representation agreement or APS, move it to a separate standalone document.
rules.notes: Fires when embedded; passes silently when standalone.

rules.rule_name: Remuneration terms affecting offer acceptance disclosed to offerors
rules.requirement: If a brokerage's agreement with a seller contains remuneration terms that may affect whether an offer to buy is accepted, the brokerage must disclose the existence and details to any person making a written offer, as soon as possible after the offer and before any offer is accepted, and make best efforts to obtain a written acknowledgement.
rules.applies_when: The listing/representation agreement contains remuneration terms that could influence offer acceptance.
rules.detection_signal: Remuneration terms of that type in the listing agreement; a corresponding disclosure to offerors (usually not in the package).
rules.finding_template: Confirm the remuneration-terms disclosure to offerors.
rules.confirm_text: I disclosed, in writing, any remuneration terms that could affect whether an offer is accepted to every person who made a written offer, before any offer was accepted.
rules.fix_guidance: Provide the written disclosure of the relevant remuneration terms to each offeror and obtain a written acknowledgement before acceptance.
rules.pinpoint: O. Reg. 567/05 s.23; TRESA Act s.33 [legal-review]
rules.notes: Overlaps Category 6.

rules.rule_name: Existence of seller's information statement disclosed to buyers
rules.requirement: If the seller's agent knows the seller completed a written statement intended to inform buyers about the property, the agent must disclose its existence to every interested buyer and make it available on request.
rules.applies_when: Seller-side representation and a seller-completed buyer-information statement exists.
rules.detection_signal: Presence of such a statement (usually outside the package).
rules.finding_template: Confirm the seller-information-statement disclosure.
rules.confirm_text: If the seller completed a written statement intended to inform buyers about the property, I disclosed its existence to every interested buyer and made it available on request.
rules.fix_guidance: Disclose that the statement exists to interested buyers and provide it on request.

rules.rule_name: Third-party goods/services disclosure and consent
rules.requirement: An agent must not, on a client's behalf, enter an agreement with a third party for goods/services to the client unless the agent has disclosed in writing to the client the subject-matter and who pays, obtained the client's consent, and disclosed in writing to the third party who is responsible for paying.
rules.applies_when: The agent arranges third-party goods/services for the client in connection with the trade.
rules.detection_signal: A third-party arrangement plus the three required disclosures/consent (rarely in the package).
rules.finding_template: Confirm the third-party goods/services disclosures and consent.
rules.confirm_text: For any third-party goods or services I arranged on my client's behalf, I disclosed the subject-matter and payer to my client in writing, obtained my client's consent, and disclosed the payer to the third party in writing.
rules.fix_guidance: Document the subject-matter and payer to the client, obtain the client's written consent, and disclose the payer to the third party in writing.

rules.rule_name: Trust deposit terms disclosed to depositor
rules.requirement: Brokerages must fully and clearly disclose in writing to a person depositing trust money the terms on which the money is held, including whether it is in an interest-bearing account and the interest rate the brokerage receives.
rules.applies_when: Trust money (e.g., a deposit) is held by the brokerage.
rules.detection_signal: A written disclosure of the trust-deposit interest terms to the depositor.
rules.finding_template: Confirm the trust-deposit terms disclosure.
rules.confirm_text: The person who deposited trust money received a written disclosure of the deposit terms, including whether the account is interest-bearing and the interest rate the brokerage receives.
rules.fix_guidance: Provide the depositor with the written trust-deposit terms disclosure.
rules.notes: Overlaps Category 8; often a brokerage-standard document.

rules.rule_name: Multiple-representation situation is documented
rules.requirement: A brokerage or designated representative must not represent more than one client in a trade unless the mandatory written multiple-representation disclosure is made (plus acknowledgement best-efforts and written consent).
rules.applies_when: The same brokerage represents both a seller and a buyer client in the trade, OR the same designated representative represents a seller and buyer, OR one DR represents competing buyers, in the same trade.
rules.detection_signal: Same brokerage and/or same designated representative on both sides of the confirmation-of-cooperation/representation documentation and the APS; presence of a multiple-representation disclosure document.
rules.finding_template: This trade appears to involve multiple representation (the same brokerage or agent on both sides). A written multiple-representation disclosure is required. Confirm it is present before submitting to your brokerage.
rules.fix_guidance: Provide the mandatory multiple-representation disclosure and obtain written consent from every affected client before proceeding.
rules.source: Bulletin 3.2; TRESA / O. Reg. 567/05; O. Reg. 365/22 (Code of Ethics)
rules.notes: Strong document-detectable trigger once OREA representation forms are loaded.

rules.rule_name: MR disclosure content is complete
rules.requirement: The multiple-representation disclosure must state the fact of multiple representation and describe the differences in duties owed, services provided, and remuneration arrangements between single vs multiple representation.
rules.applies_when: Multiple representation applies (3.2-01) and a disclosure document is present.
rules.detection_signal: The disclosure covers the fact of MR and the differences in duties, services, and remuneration.
rules.finding_template: The multiple-representation disclosure may be missing required content (the fact of multiple representation and the differences in duties, services, and remuneration). Review before submitting.
rules.fix_guidance: Ensure the disclosure spells out the fact of multiple representation and the specific differences in duties, services, and remuneration.
rules.notes: Depends on the disclosure being captured as legible text (OCR quality).

rules.rule_name: MR disclosure advises independent professional advice
rules.requirement: In multiple representation the brokerage must advise the client to seek independent professional advice before consenting.
rules.applies_when: Multiple representation applies and a disclosure is present.
rules.detection_signal: Language advising the client to seek independent professional advice.
rules.finding_template: The multiple-representation disclosure does not appear to advise the client to seek independent professional advice. Confirm this is included.
rules.fix_guidance: Add clear language advising the client to obtain independent professional advice before consenting.

rules.rule_name: Written consent to multiple representation from every client
rules.requirement: After disclosure, if each client agrees, each must provide written consent before the brokerage/DR continues to represent them in the trade.
rules.applies_when: Multiple representation applies.
rules.detection_signal: A signed, dated written consent to multiple representation from each affected client.
rules.finding_template: Written consent to multiple representation is missing for one or more clients. Every affected client must consent in writing before proceeding.
rules.fix_guidance: Obtain signed written consent from each affected client before continuing to act.
rules.notes: Signature/date presence is deterministic; matching each client is AI-judgment.

rules.rule_name: Acknowledgement of receipt of MR disclosure (best efforts)
rules.requirement: The agent must make best efforts to obtain a written acknowledgement from each client that the MR disclosure was received, and provide a copy if made.
rules.applies_when: Multiple representation applies.
rules.detection_signal: A signed acknowledgement of receipt of the MR disclosure.
rules.finding_template: No written acknowledgement that the multiple-representation disclosure was received is on file. This is a best-efforts requirement — confirm one was requested.
rules.fix_guidance: Obtain a written acknowledgement of receipt from each client and keep a copy in the file.
rules.notes: Best-efforts → Warning, not Critical.

rules.rule_name: MR disclosure/consent timing
rules.requirement: Disclosure and consent must occur as soon as the brokerage/agent is aware of more than one client in the trade; disclosure/consent at the time an offer is submitted is, in almost all circumstances, too late.
rules.applies_when: Multiple representation applies and dates are available.
rules.detection_signal: Date of the MR disclosure/consent relative to the offer and agreement dates.
rules.finding_template: The multiple-representation disclosure/consent may have been made at or after the offer stage, which is generally too late. Confirm timing.
rules.fix_guidance: Ensure the disclosure and consent are dated as soon as multiple representation arose, before proceeding.
rules.notes: Inferable only when reliable dates are present.

rules.rule_name: Seller-client + buyer-client disclosed to competing buyers
rules.requirement: If a brokerage has a seller client and a buyer client in the same trade, it must disclose this fact to every other buyer who makes a written offer, as soon as possible after the offer is received and before any offer is accepted, and make best efforts to obtain a written acknowledgement. (Distinct from the MR disclosure; applies even with different designated representatives.)
rules.applies_when: Brokerage has a seller client and a buyer client in the same trade AND competing written offers exist from other buyers.
rules.detection_signal: Competing offers from other buyers (usually not in the submitted package) plus a disclosure to those buyers.
rules.finding_template: Confirm the seller-client/buyer-client disclosure to competing buyers.
rules.confirm_text: Where my brokerage had both a seller client and a buyer client in this trade, I disclosed that fact in writing to every other buyer who made a written offer, before any offer was accepted.
rules.fix_guidance: Disclose the seller-client/buyer-client fact in writing to each competing buyer (via their agent if any) before acceptance and seek an acknowledgement.
rules.notes: Competing-offer context is rarely in the package → Confirm. Frequently missed — strong bounce-back candidate.

rules.rule_name: Financial benefit disclosed to client
rules.requirement: An agent must disclose to their client all direct and indirect financial benefits the agent, or a person related to the agent, might receive in connection with services to the client, as soon as the agent knows or ought to know a benefit might be received.
rules.applies_when: The agent or a related person may receive any benefit (payment, gift, tickets, future service, referral value) beyond the client's contracted remuneration, in connection with the trade.
rules.detection_signal: A referral/benefit arrangement (almost never in the package) plus a financial-benefit disclosure.
rules.finding_template: Confirm the financial-benefit disclosure.
rules.confirm_text: I disclosed to my client every direct or indirect financial benefit that I, or a person related to me, might receive in connection with services to my client (including referrals to a lender, inspector, lawyer, mover, stager, or similar).
rules.fix_guidance: Provide a written financial-benefit disclosure to your client covering the benefit (see content rule 3.3-02).
rules.source: Bulletin 3.3; TRESA / O. Reg. 567/05; O. Reg. 365/22 (Code of Ethics)

rules.rule_name: Financial benefit disclosure content complete
rules.requirement: The disclosure must state: what the benefit is (estimated value/amount, conditions, direct or indirect); who might receive it; how the agent is related to that person; and the relationship between the benefit provider and the agent/related person.
rules.applies_when: A financial-benefit disclosure is present in the package (i.e., 3.3-01 affirmed or a disclosure document is found).
rules.detection_signal: The disclosure covers all four content elements.
rules.finding_template: The financial-benefit disclosure may be missing required content (value/conditions, who receives it, the relationship, and the provider relationship). Review before submitting.
rules.fix_guidance: Ensure the disclosure answers: what the benefit is, who receives it, the agent's relationship to that person, and the relationship to the provider.
rules.notes: Dependent on 3.3-01 / presence of a disclosure document.

rules.rule_name: Acknowledgement of financial-benefit disclosure (best efforts)
rules.requirement: The agent must make best efforts to obtain a written acknowledgement that the financial-benefit disclosure was received, and provide a copy if made.
rules.applies_when: A financial-benefit disclosure applies.
rules.detection_signal: A signed acknowledgement of receipt.
rules.finding_template: No written acknowledgement of the financial-benefit disclosure is on file. This is best-efforts — confirm one was requested.
rules.fix_guidance: Obtain a written acknowledgement and keep a copy in the file.

rules.rule_name: No payment from a source other than the employing brokerage
rules.requirement: An agent is prohibited from receiving payment directly from any source other than the brokerage that employs them.
rules.applies_when: Any payment to the agent connected with the trade.
rules.detection_signal: Direct payment to the agent from a party other than the employing brokerage (not evidenced in the package).
rules.finding_template: Confirm the source-of-payment rule.
rules.confirm_text: I have not received, and will not receive, payment for this trade directly from any source other than my employing brokerage.
rules.fix_guidance: Route all agent compensation through the employing brokerage.
rules.notes: Conduct rule; Confirm attestation.

rules.rule_name: Multiple agreements / seller-paid buyer fees disclosed
rules.requirement: Where the brokerage will receive remuneration under more than one agreement in the same trade, the terms must be disclosed to both affected parties; the brokerage is prohibited from collecting under more than one agreement for the same trade unless that disclosure is made. Includes the seller offering to pay all/part of the buyer's brokerage fees.
rules.applies_when: The APS or related agreements show the seller paying some/all of the buyer's brokerage fees, or the brokerage collecting under more than one agreement.
rules.detection_signal: APS clauses assigning buyer brokerage fees to the seller, or dual-agreement remuneration; a disclosure of those terms to both parties.
rules.finding_template: This deal appears to involve remuneration under more than one agreement (for example, the seller paying part of the buyer's brokerage fees). Those terms must be disclosed to both parties. Confirm the disclosure is present.
rules.fix_guidance: Disclose the remuneration terms in both the buyer's and seller's agreements to both affected parties before collecting.
rules.pinpoint: O. Reg. 567/05 s.23; TRESA Act s.33 [legal-review]
rules.notes: Detectable in the APS → Critical. Overlaps Category 6. Strong bounce-back candidate.

rules.rule_name: Personal-trade written notice to all parties
rules.requirement: Before an agent is involved in a personal transaction (acquiring or divesting any interest in real estate, or offering to), they must provide the required written notice to all parties to the agreement before making or receiving any offer.
rules.applies_when: The agent is a principal (buyer or seller) in the trade, represented or not.
rules.detection_signal: The agent's name matches a party on the APS (unreliable without an agent roster); presence of the personal-trade notice.
rules.finding_template: Confirm the personal-trade notice.
rules.confirm_text: If I am a party to this transaction (a personal trade), I provided the required written notice to all parties before any offer was made or received.
rules.fix_guidance: Provide the required written personal-trade notice to every party before making or receiving an offer.
rules.source: Bulletin 3.4; Bulletin 1.3 (notice requirements); TRESA / O. Reg. 567/05
rules.notes: Becomes auto-detectable once an agent roster/identity is available; Confirm for now.

rules.rule_name: Personal-trade notice content complete
rules.requirement: The written notice must include: a statement that the agent is a salesperson or broker; full disclosure of all facts within the agent's knowledge that affect or will affect the value; and (when acquiring) details of any negotiation/offer/agreement for onward disposition of the agent's interest.
rules.applies_when: A personal-trade notice is present in the package.
rules.detection_signal: The notice covers the three content elements.
rules.finding_template: The personal-trade notice may be missing required content (registrant status, all value-affecting facts, and onward-disposition details if acquiring). Review before submitting.
rules.fix_guidance: Ensure the notice states you are a registrant, discloses all value-affecting facts you know, and covers any onward-sale arrangement if you are acquiring.
rules.notes: Dependent on 3.4-01 / presence of a notice.

rules.rule_name: Personal-trade notice acknowledged by each party
rules.requirement: Written acknowledgement of receipt of the personal-trade notice must be obtained from each party to the agreement before proceeding.
rules.applies_when: A personal trade applies (notice present or 3.4-01 affirmed).
rules.detection_signal: A signed acknowledgement from each party.
rules.finding_template: A signed acknowledgement of the personal-trade notice is missing for one or more parties. Each party must acknowledge before proceeding.
rules.fix_guidance: Obtain a written acknowledgement from every party before proceeding.
rules.notes: This is a *mandatory* notice acknowledgement (Critical), stricter than the best-efforts acknowledgements elsewhere.

rules.rule_name: Agent does not represent a party to their own personal trade
rules.requirement: An agent must not represent a party to their own personal trade — the conflict is too severe to manage.
rules.applies_when: The agent is a principal in the trade.
rules.detection_signal: The agent appears as both a party and a representing agent in the same trade (unreliable without identity match).
rules.finding_template: Confirm you are not representing a party to your own trade.
rules.confirm_text: I am not acting as the representing agent for any party in a transaction to which I am also a party.
rules.fix_guidance: Ensure another brokerage/agent represents any party; do not represent a party to your own trade.
rules.notes: Auto-detectable once identity matching is available.

rules.rule_name: Property-interest disclosure
rules.requirement: Where an agent represents a client and the agent, a related person, the agent's PREC, or a person related to the PREC has or may have an interest in the property, the agent must disclose the interest to the client and to every person making or receiving an offer, as soon as possible after knowing/ought-to-knowing and before any offer.
rules.applies_when: The agent represents a client and a property interest of the agent/related person/PREC exists in the subject property.
rules.detection_signal: An ownership/interest link between the agent (or related person/PREC) and the property (rarely in the package); presence of a property-interest disclosure.
rules.finding_template: Confirm the property-interest disclosure.
rules.confirm_text: If I, a person related to me, or my personal real estate corporation has or may have an interest in this property, I disclosed that interest to my client and to every person making or receiving an offer, before any offer.
rules.fix_guidance: Provide the property-interest disclosure to your client and to each offeror/offeree before any offer.
rules.notes: Broader than the personal-trade notice (captures related persons and PREC).

rules.rule_name: Property-interest disclosure content complete
rules.requirement: The disclosure must describe the property interest with enough information for the recipient to understand its nature and any conflict/potential conflict, and — if a person other than the agent holds it — describe the relationship between the agent and that person.
rules.applies_when: A property-interest disclosure is present in the package.
rules.detection_signal: The disclosure describes the interest, the conflict, and the relationship (if applicable).
rules.finding_template: The property-interest disclosure may be missing required content (a clear description of the interest, the conflict, and the relationship). Review before submitting.
rules.fix_guidance: Ensure the disclosure explains the interest, the potential conflict, and the relationship to any related holder.
rules.notes: Dependent on 3.4-05 / presence of a disclosure.

rules.rule_name: Property-interest disclosure acknowledged (best efforts)
rules.requirement: After making the property-interest disclosure the agent must use best efforts to obtain an acknowledgement from each recipient and provide a copy if made.
rules.applies_when: A property-interest disclosure applies.
rules.detection_signal: A signed acknowledgement from each recipient.
rules.finding_template: No acknowledgement of the property-interest disclosure is on file. This is best-efforts — confirm one was requested.
rules.fix_guidance: Obtain a written acknowledgement from each recipient and keep a copy.
rules.notes: Contrast with the mandatory personal-trade notice acknowledgement (3.4-03).

rules.rule_name: Conflict handled through the required four steps
rules.requirement: If any actual or potential conflict of interest arises, the agent must not provide further services until they have (1) disclosed the conflict, (2) advised the client to seek independent professional advice, (3) taken steps to ensure the client understands the conflict, and (4) obtained the client's consent to receive/continue services.
rules.applies_when: Any actual or potential conflict not already covered by the specific rules (multiple representation, financial benefits, personal trades, property interests).
rules.detection_signal: Indicators of a conflict (generally not machine-detectable); a conflict disclosure and written consent.
rules.finding_template: Confirm conflict-of-interest handling.
rules.confirm_text: For any other conflict or potential conflict of interest in this deal, I disclosed it, advised my client to seek independent professional advice, confirmed my client understood it, and obtained my client's written consent before continuing.
rules.fix_guidance: Complete all four steps — disclose, advise independent advice, confirm understanding, obtain written consent — before providing further services.
rules.source: Bulletin 3.5; O. Reg. 365/22 (Code of Ethics — conflicts of interest); TRESA
rules.notes: Open-ended conflicts are the least document-detectable in the category. The specific conflicts are handled by 3.2/3.3/3.4. This umbrella attestation absorbs the "verify understanding" step.

rules.rule_name: Conflict disclosure content
rules.requirement: The conflict disclosure must include the circumstances giving rise to the conflict (and, where applicable, the relationship causing it) and be clear and complete enough for an informed decision.
rules.applies_when: A conflict disclosure is present in the package.
rules.detection_signal: The disclosure describes the circumstances and any relevant relationship.
rules.finding_template: The conflict-of-interest disclosure may not clearly describe the circumstances and relationship behind the conflict. Review before submitting.
rules.fix_guidance: Ensure the disclosure explains the circumstances and any relationship that creates the conflict, in clear and complete terms.
rules.notes: Dependent on presence of a conflict disclosure.

rules.rule_name: Client advised to seek independent professional advice
rules.requirement: After disclosure the agent must advise the client to seek independent professional advice and explain they cannot advise on the conflict itself.
rules.applies_when: A conflict disclosure is present.
rules.detection_signal: Language advising independent professional advice.
rules.finding_template: The conflict disclosure does not appear to advise the client to seek independent professional advice. Confirm this is included.
rules.fix_guidance: Include clear language advising the client to obtain independent professional advice.
rules.notes: Auto-check parallel to 3.2-03; the manual side is covered by the 3.5-01 attestation.

rules.rule_name: Written consent to continue despite conflict
rules.requirement: The agent may provide/continue services only after obtaining the client's consent; if the client does not consent, the agent must not proceed.
rules.applies_when: A conflict disclosure is present.
rules.detection_signal: A signed, dated consent to continue receiving services despite the disclosed conflict.
rules.finding_template: Written consent to continue despite the disclosed conflict is missing. Without it, services must not continue.
rules.fix_guidance: Obtain the client's written consent to proceed despite the conflict before continuing.
rules.notes: Dependent on presence of a conflict disclosure.

rules.rule_name: Number of competing offers communicated to every offeror
rules.requirement: The number of competing written offers must be communicated to every person making one of the offers. (Verbal or unsubmitted offers are not competing offers.)
rules.applies_when: Competing written offers were received on the property.
rules.detection_signal: Communication conduct; not in the accepted package.
rules.finding_template: Confirm the number of competing offers was communicated.
rules.confirm_text: I communicated the number of competing written offers to every person who made one of the offers.
rules.fix_guidance: Tell every offeror how many competing written offers there are.

rules.rule_name: Content of competing offers shared only per written direction
rules.requirement: Without the seller's written direction, the seller's agent must not share the content of offers. If the seller directs in writing, the specified content must be shared with every person making an offer.
rules.applies_when: Competing offers exist and content sharing was considered or done.
rules.detection_signal: Sharing conduct + the seller's written direction (Form 244/209 may be in the file).
rules.finding_template: Confirm content-sharing followed the seller's written direction.
rules.confirm_text: I shared the content of competing offers only as the seller directed in writing, and where the seller so directed, I shared the specified content with every person making an offer.
rules.fix_guidance: Only share offer content with a signed seller direction identifying exactly what may be shared; share it with all offerors.
rules.notes: Written direction ties to OREA Form 209 (Seller Direction to Share Substance of Offers) / 244.

rules.rule_name: No personal or identifying information of an offeror shared
rules.requirement: An agent must not share the personal information of a person making an offer or any information that would identify them. The seller cannot lawfully direct otherwise.
rules.applies_when: Competing offers exist.
rules.detection_signal: Conduct; not in the package.
rules.finding_template: Confirm no offeror's personal/identifying information was shared.
rules.confirm_text: I did not share the personal or identifying information of any person making an offer, and I did not act on any direction to do so.
rules.fix_guidance: Never disclose an offeror's identity or personal information, even if the seller asks.
rules.notes: A hard prohibition — the seller cannot override it.

rules.rule_name: Offer Summary Document complete (if present)
rules.requirement: Where an Offer Summary Document is used to record an offer, it should be complete and accurately reflect the offer. (RECO requests offers or summary documents when reviewing an offer process.)
rules.applies_when: An Offer Summary Document (OREA Form 801) is present in the package.
rules.detection_signal: Presence of the Offer Summary Document and whether it is complete.
rules.finding_template: Confirm the Offer Summary Document is complete.
rules.confirm_text: Any Offer Summary Document used for this trade is complete and accurately reflects the offer.
rules.fix_guidance: Complete the Offer Summary Document for each summarized offer.
rules.source: Bulletin 4.2 (RECO requests offers/summary documents). OREA Form 801 (Offer Summary Document).
rules.pinpoint: Practice/RECO documentation (OREA Form 801); no direct section
rules.notes: Matches the SPIS pattern (7.4-03): if present, check completeness; if absent, no finding. Built assuming Form 801 may be in the package, but **held as Confirm until Step 2.4 validates inclusion; graduate to Warning once confirmed.**

rules.rule_name: Offers conveyed promptly unless a written direction to delay exists
rules.requirement: A seller's agent must convey an offer to the seller as soon as possible after receiving it, unless the seller has given a clear, specific, signed written direction to defer consideration to a stated date and time.
rules.applies_when: Any trade where offers were received (especially a delayed-offer process).
rules.detection_signal: Timing conduct; the written direction may be in the file.
rules.finding_template: Confirm prompt conveyance / valid delay direction.
rules.confirm_text: I conveyed every offer to the seller as soon as possible after receiving it, unless the seller gave a clear, specific, signed written direction to delay presentation to a stated date and time.
rules.fix_guidance: Convey offers immediately unless you hold a specific signed written direction to delay.

rules.rule_name: Seller's offer-process direction is specific and complete (if present)
rules.requirement: Where a delayed-offer or other special offer process is used, the seller's written direction must be specific and detailed — covering the presentation date/time and explicit pre-emptive-offer instructions — signed and dated. A brief general instruction or a listing note like "seller reserves the right to view pre-emptive offers without notice" does NOT satisfy the obligation.
rules.applies_when: A seller's written direction re offers (Form 244 / 224) is in the package.
rules.detection_signal: Presence of the direction and whether it is specific, signed, and dated (vs. a vague general statement).
rules.finding_template: Confirm the seller's offer-process direction is specific and complete.
rules.confirm_text: Where a delayed-offer or special offer process was used, the seller's written direction is specific and signed — it covers the presentation date/time and how pre-emptive offers are handled — and is not merely a general "reserves the right to view pre-emptive offers" statement.
rules.fix_guidance: Replace any vague direction with a specific, signed, dated written direction covering the presentation date/time and explicit pre-emptive-offer handling.
rules.source: Bulletin 4.2; Bulletin 4.3. OREA Form 244 (Seller's Direction re: Property/Offers) / 224.
rules.notes: Built assuming Form 244/224 is in the package, but **held as Confirm until Step 2.4 validates form inclusion against real pilot deal packages; graduate to Warning (AI-judgment) once consistent inclusion is confirmed.**

rules.rule_name: Interested parties notified on any change of direction
rules.requirement: If the seller changes the offer-presentation direction, it must be documented in a new signed written direction, listing notes/online platforms updated immediately, and all interested parties notified in writing (interested = booked showings, viewed the property, said they'd offer, or submitted an offer).
rules.applies_when: The seller changed the offer-presentation direction during the process.
rules.detection_signal: Notification conduct; not in the accepted package.
rules.finding_template: Confirm notification on any change of offer direction.
rules.confirm_text: Whenever the seller changed the offer-presentation direction, I documented it in a new signed written direction, updated the listing notes/online platforms, and notified all interested parties in writing.
rules.fix_guidance: On any change, get a new signed direction, update all listings, and notify every interested party in writing.
rules.notes: Email and text are acceptable written notice.

rules.rule_name: Pre-emptive offers handled per the seller's written direction
rules.requirement: A seller's agent must have specific signed written instructions on how to manage pre-emptive offers (including any price/condition thresholds and whether/when the seller is informed), and must follow them.
rules.applies_when: A delayed-offer or conditioned process where a pre-emptive offer could arise or did arise.
rules.detection_signal: Handling conduct; the written direction may be in the file.
rules.finding_template: Confirm pre-emptive-offer handling followed the seller's written direction.
rules.confirm_text: I handled any pre-emptive (bully) offer strictly per the seller's specific signed written direction, including any price/condition thresholds and the required notifications.
rules.fix_guidance: Obtain specific signed instructions covering pre-emptive-offer scenarios and follow them exactly.
rules.notes: Direction must cover explicit scenarios (e.g., "only review offers above $X"; notify interested parties if the seller chooses to review).

rules.rule_name: Multiple representation disclosed on an own-client pre-emptive offer
rules.requirement: A seller's agent whose own buyer client makes a pre-emptive offer must deal in good faith, apprise other interested parties of that fact as soon as possible, and disclose the multiple representation to all prospective buyers.
rules.applies_when: The seller's agent (or brokerage) represents the buyer making a pre-emptive offer on the same property.
rules.detection_signal: Same brokerage/agent on both sides is partly detectable (confirmation of cooperation), but the good-faith notification is conduct.
rules.finding_template: Confirm MR disclosure and good-faith notice on an own-client pre-emptive offer.
rules.confirm_text: Where my own buyer client made a pre-emptive offer on this property, I disclosed the multiple representation to all prospective buyers and apprised other interested parties as soon as possible.
rules.fix_guidance: Disclose the multiple representation to all prospective buyers and notify interested parties; follow Category 3.2 for the MR consent forms.
rules.source: Bulletin 4.3; Bulletin 3.2 (multiple representation). OREA Forms 325/326 (MR consent).
rules.notes: Strong cross-reference to Category 3.2 — the MR disclosure/consent obligations there apply.

rules.rule_name: Remuneration clause states amount and payor/recipient
rules.requirement: Where the APS contains a remuneration clause (the seller compensating the buyer for brokerage fees), the clause must state the **amount** to be paid and the **payor and recipient** (including whether disbursement is through the seller's brokerage or lawyer). Absent either, the clause is unenforceable as a compensation obligation.
rules.applies_when: A seller-pays-buyer-brokerage-fee remuneration clause is present in the APS.
rules.detection_signal: The clause and whether it states a payment amount and identifies payor/recipient + disbursement.
rules.finding_template: The remuneration clause in the APS is missing the amount and/or who pays and receives it — without these it is unenforceable. Fix before submitting.
rules.fix_guidance: State the exact amount and identify the payor, recipient, and how it is disbursed (seller's brokerage or lawyer).
rules.pinpoint: O. Reg. 567/05 s.23; TRESA Act s.33 [legal-review]
rules.notes: Escalated to Critical per round-2 calibration: missing amount or payor makes the clause unenforceable, not merely incomplete. Cross-ref 3.1-04 (if these terms may affect offer acceptance they must also be disclosed to offerors — owned by Category 3).

rules.rule_name: Remuneration clause states purpose, tax treatment, and timing
rules.requirement: The remuneration clause should also state its **purpose** (seller compensates buyer for brokerage fees owed under the buyer representation agreement), the **tax treatment** of the amount, and the **timing** (payment due date, e.g. on completion).
rules.applies_when: A seller-pays-buyer-fee remuneration clause is present in the APS.
rules.detection_signal: Whether the clause covers purpose, tax treatment, and timing.
rules.finding_template: The remuneration clause may be missing its purpose, tax treatment, or payment timing. Review before submitting.
rules.fix_guidance: Add the purpose, the tax treatment of the amount, and the payment due date to the clause.
rules.notes: These three components are completeness items (the clause still functions without them) → Warning. Companion to the Critical core check in 6.2-01.

rules.rule_name: Buyer representation agreement addresses excess/shortfall
rules.requirement: When the seller offers to compensate the buyer's brokerage fees, the buyer representation agreement should address the variance: if the seller offers **more** than the buyer's commitment (buyer reduces payment to match, retains the excess, or brokerage receives the full amount); if **less** (buyer owes the shortfall, brokerage accepts the reduced amount, or another arrangement).
rules.applies_when: A seller-pays-buyer-fee arrangement exists and a buyer representation agreement is in the package.
rules.detection_signal: Whether the buyer representation agreement covers the excess/shortfall scenarios.
rules.finding_template: The buyer representation agreement may not address what happens if the seller's fee contribution differs from the buyer's commitment (excess or shortfall). Review before submitting.
rules.fix_guidance: Add terms covering both the excess and shortfall cases to the buyer representation agreement.
rules.notes: The buyer-side counterpart of the rep-agreement remuneration-change content (2.3-07, owned by Category 2). Cross-reference, not a restatement.

rules.rule_name: No remuneration charged to a self-represented seller
rules.requirement: Brokerages must not enter into an agreement with a self-represented seller to provide assistance, or charge or collect remuneration for the provision of assistance. A self-represented seller may voluntarily compensate the buyer via a remuneration clause, but cannot be charged by the brokerage.
rules.applies_when: The trade involves a self-represented seller.
rules.detection_signal: A charge to a self-represented seller is generally not in the accepted package; detectable only if a service/commission agreement with the SRP seller is included.
rules.finding_template: Confirm no remuneration was charged to a self-represented seller.
rules.confirm_text: I did not charge or collect remuneration from a self-represented seller for assistance; any seller contribution to the buyer's brokerage fees was voluntary via a remuneration clause.
rules.fix_guidance: Never charge a self-represented seller; if the seller is to receive services, enter a representation agreement and treat them as a client.
rules.pinpoint: TRESA Act (agreement must include representation) [legal-review]; O. Reg. 567/05 s.13.5
rules.notes: Becomes a detectable Warning/Critical if a commission/service agreement signed by a self-represented seller appears in the package.

rules.rule_name: Multiple representation handled where the arrangement creates it
rules.requirement: Entering a representation agreement with a seller — particularly one who intended to be self-represented — to enable a remuneration arrangement requires full multiple-representation disclosure, a recommendation to seek independent professional advice, and written consent from both parties before proceeding. The agent bears the burden of proving the arrangement serves the buyer's best interests.
rules.applies_when: A seller-pays-buyer-fee arrangement results in the same brokerage representing both parties (or converts a self-represented seller into a client).
rules.detection_signal: Same brokerage on both sides is partly detectable; the disclosure/consent obligations are owned by Category 3.2.
rules.finding_template: Confirm multiple-representation handling for the remuneration arrangement.
rules.confirm_text: Where the remuneration arrangement created multiple representation, I made the full MR disclosure, recommended independent professional advice, and obtained written consent from both parties before proceeding.
rules.fix_guidance: Follow the Category 3.2 multiple-representation steps (OREA 325/326) before proceeding.
rules.notes: Cross-reference to Category 3.2 (canonical owner of multiple representation).

rules.rule_name: Material facts determined and disclosed to client
rules.requirement: Four-step duty: take reasonable steps to determine material facts (not merely accept the seller's verbal representations); promptly disclose them to the client; advise the client to consider whether they affect their decision; make best efforts to obtain an acknowledgement.
rules.applies_when: Any trade (buyer or seller side).
rules.detection_signal: Determination/disclosure of material facts is conduct tied to this property; whether a material fact exists can't be read from the package.
rules.finding_template: Confirm material-facts disclosure to your client.
rules.confirm_text: I took reasonable steps to determine the material facts about this property (beyond the seller's verbal representations), promptly disclosed them to my client, and advised my client to consider how they might affect their decision.
rules.fix_guidance: Research and verify material facts, disclose them to your client in writing, and advise on their impact.
rules.notes: Material-fact examples: knob-and-tube wiring, galvanized/lead plumbing, system age/condition, flood/fire/structural history, unpermitted renovations, zoning, former grow-op, rights-of-way, nearby nuisances.

rules.rule_name: Material-facts disclosure acknowledged (best efforts)
rules.requirement: Make best efforts to obtain a written acknowledgement that the material-facts disclosure and advice were received, and provide a copy if made.
rules.applies_when: A material-facts disclosure to the client is on file.
rules.detection_signal: A signed acknowledgement of the material-facts disclosure.
rules.finding_template: No acknowledgement of a material-facts disclosure is on file. This is best-efforts — confirm one was requested.
rules.fix_guidance: Obtain the client's written acknowledgement and keep a copy.
rules.notes: Only meaningful when a material-facts disclosure document exists in the file.

rules.rule_name: Seller-obligated facts / latent defects disclosed to buyers
rules.requirement: If the seller's agent is aware of a fact the seller is legally obligated to disclose (notably a latent defect — one making the property unfit for habitation, dangerous, or potentially dangerous and not apparent on reasonable inspection), the agent must disclose it to every buyer who expresses an interest.
rules.applies_when: Seller-side representation where the agent is aware of a seller-obligated fact or latent defect.
rules.detection_signal: Awareness of a latent defect is conduct tied to this property; not in the package.
rules.finding_template: Confirm disclosure of any seller-obligated facts / latent defects.
rules.confirm_text: Where I (as the seller's agent) was aware of a fact the seller is legally obligated to disclose — such as a known latent defect — I disclosed it to every buyer who expressed an interest in the property.
rules.fix_guidance: Disclose known latent defects to every interested buyer; advise the seller to seek a legal opinion on what qualifies.
rules.source: Bulletin 7.4 (based on case law, not TRESA)
rules.notes: Patent defects need not be disclosed (buyer-beware) but must not be concealed; latent defects must be disclosed. Non-disclosure can be misrepresentation.

rules.rule_name: Latent-defect disclosure acknowledged (best efforts)
rules.requirement: Make best efforts to obtain a written acknowledgement from each buyer who receives the disclosure, and provide a copy if made.
rules.applies_when: A seller-obligated-fact / latent-defect disclosure to buyers is on file.
rules.detection_signal: A signed acknowledgement from each buyer receiving the disclosure.
rules.finding_template: No buyer acknowledgement of a seller-disclosure is on file. This is best-efforts — confirm one was requested.
rules.fix_guidance: Obtain each buyer's written acknowledgement and keep copies.

rules.rule_name: Seller disclosure document present and complete (if used)
rules.requirement: Where the package includes a Seller Property Information Statement (SPIS) or a Seller Disclosure – Latent Defect(s) form, it should be complete, signed, and dated, and its existence disclosed to interested buyers (see 3.1-05).
rules.applies_when: A SPIS (OREA 220-series) or Seller Disclosure – Latent Defect(s) (OREA 299) is present in the package.
rules.detection_signal: Presence of the form and whether it is signed/dated and complete.
rules.finding_template: A seller disclosure statement is in the package but appears incomplete or unsigned. Review before submitting.
rules.fix_guidance: Ensure the SPIS / latent-defect disclosure is complete, signed, dated, and its existence disclosed to buyers.
rules.source: Bulletin 7.4; Bulletin 7.3; Bulletin 3.1 (existence-disclosure). OREA Forms 220–222 / 225 (SPIS), 299 (Latent Defect).
rules.notes: The one genuinely document-detectable rule in this category. SPIS is voluntary — its absence is not a finding; only its incompleteness when present is.

rules.rule_name: Stigma handled
rules.requirement: Stigmas are not legislated, but the agent's best-interests duty applies. For seller clients with a possible stigmatizing issue, advise legal advice and obtain written instructions on disclosure; for buyer clients, discuss sensitivities and address them (a protective clause where appropriate).
rules.applies_when: Any trade.
rules.detection_signal: Conduct/discussion tied to this property; not in the package.
rules.finding_template: Confirm stigma was addressed with your client.
rules.confirm_text: I discussed potential stigmas with my client; for a seller client with a possible stigmatizing issue I advised them to seek legal advice and obtained written instructions on disclosure, and for a buyer client I discussed their sensitivities and addressed them (including a protective clause where appropriate).
rules.fix_guidance: Have a frank stigma conversation with the client; document seller instructions or buyer protective clauses.
rules.notes: Examples: on-property death, notorious former owner, reputed haunting, former (remediated) grow-op, crime use. Impact is buyer-specific; no fixed disclosure list.

rules.rule_name: APS deposit clause states amount and deposit holder
rules.requirement: The APS deposit provision must state the **deposit amount** and name the **deposit holder**. Absent either, the deposit obligation is unenforceable.
rules.applies_when: An APS with a deposit is present.
rules.detection_signal: The deposit clause on the APS and whether the amount and deposit holder are filled in.
rules.finding_template: The APS deposit clause is missing the deposit amount and/or the named deposit holder — without these the deposit obligation is unenforceable. Fix before submitting.
rules.fix_guidance: Fill in the deposit amount and name the deposit holder in the APS.
rules.source: APS (OREA Form 100 deposit provision); TRESA / O. Reg. 567/05 (trust money). _Pinpoint section in the legislation pass._
rules.pinpoint: APS (OREA Form 100 deposit provision); O. Reg. 567/05 s.22.11, s.17
rules.notes: Escalated to Critical per round-5 calibration, parallel to 6.2-01 (missing amount/payor). Enforceability core of the deposit provision.

rules.rule_name: APS deposit clause states held-in-trust / interest terms
rules.requirement: The deposit provision should specify that the deposit is **held in trust** and the **interest terms** (non-interest-bearing unless otherwise agreed).
rules.applies_when: An APS with a deposit is present.
rules.detection_signal: Whether the clause specifies held-in-trust and interest terms.
rules.finding_template: The APS deposit clause may not specify the held-in-trust / interest terms. Review before submitting.
rules.fix_guidance: State that the deposit is held in trust and the interest terms.
rules.source: APS (OREA Form 100 deposit provision); TRESA / O. Reg. 567/05. _Pinpoint section in the legislation pass._
rules.notes: Completeness item (the deposit obligation still functions) → Warning. Deposit-**terms disclosure** to the depositor (interest-bearing? rate?) is owned by **3.1-07** — cross-ref, not restated.

rules.rule_name: Deposit placed in the brokerage's real estate trust account
rules.requirement: The deposit received for this trade must be delivered to and held in the deposit holder's real estate trust account in accordance with the APS and the legislation (within the required time).
rules.applies_when: A deposit was received for the trade.
rules.detection_signal: Whether/when the deposit was actually deposited is a trust-account record, not in the deal package.
rules.finding_template: Confirm the deposit was placed in trust as required.
rules.confirm_text: The deposit for this trade was delivered to and held in the deposit holder's real estate trust account in accordance with the agreement and the required timeframe.
rules.fix_guidance: Ensure the deposit is deposited into the brokerage's real estate trust account within the required time and held per the APS.
rules.source: TRESA / O. Reg. 567/05 (trust money). _Pinpoint section in the legislation pass._
rules.notes: Transaction-tied but not document-detectable (the trust record lives outside the deal package) → Confirm.
